# ConfigHub plugin and confighub mini

> The ConfigHub plugin for Claude Code and Codex records each configuration value an agent changes, with the request and the reason, and tells the next agent before it undoes an earlier change. confighub mini is ConfigHub, a server that keeps configuration with every change and holds production for a person's approval, made small enough to run on a laptop, in a sandbox or in a CI job, with no account. In Claude Code, a person asks for an app "using ConfigHub", or asks to attach ConfigHub to an app they have, and the agent starts a hub and makes a base, a staging copy that takes changes at once, and a live copy that changes only when the person approves with `cub mini approve`. The plugin is MIT-licensed; install it with `claude plugin marketplace add confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin` and `claude plugin install confighub@confighub`.

Pick a page by what the person is doing. Commands and outputs on these pages are from released versions; the plugin's version is in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.

Read [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/AGENTS.md) first: what the project is, what an agent may and may not do, the commands, and which page answers which question.

Then read the matching walkthrough in [the walkthroughs index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/README.md): one page for each tool, starter and user story, each with an "Agent" section written for an agent doing that job for a person.

An agent in Claude Code with the plugin also has its skill, [app-with-confighub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/plugins/confighub/skills/app-with-confighub/SKILL.md): the commands to run for an app with ConfigHub, and what it must not do. [The plugin's own README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/plugins/confighub/README.md) has the slash commands and settings, in short.

## Walkthroughs

- [cub mini](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/tool-cub-mini.md): The dozen `cub mini` commands a newcomer needs, on one small app, each next to the plain `cub` commands it stands for
- [The plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/tool-plugin.md): What your agents changed in configuration and why, the warning before one undoes another, and each `/confighub:` command; then the step to a hub
- [daytona: a sandbox experiment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/starter-daytona.md): Return a proposed change with its reason and leave production unchanged
- [kustomize-argocd: a Kustomize app that Argo CD deploys](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/starter-kustomize-argocd.md): Argo CD on a local kind cluster takes production from the hub with no pod restarted, and only what you approve
- [kustomize-flux: a Kustomize app that Flux deploys](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/starter-kustomize-flux.md): Flux on a local kind cluster takes production from the hub with no pod restarted, and only what you approve
- [parameter-store: an app that reads AWS Parameter Store](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/starter-parameter-store.md): Production's parameters written only from the revision you approved; the encrypted value never leaves Parameter Store (local stand-in)
- [vercel: an app on Vercel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/starter-vercel.md): The Vercel project's production settings written only from the revision you approved (local stand-in)
- [web: a small web service with a .env](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/starter-web.md): Deploy, update, undo, move to a shared hub and delete, each with the commands it takes
- [1. Dan: "I don't know what's wrong. Please fix it."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-01-find-the-fault.md): Find the fault in a customer's platform, keep the two changes they meant with their reasons, and hand it back as files for their Git
- [2. George's colleague: "Run my app, and keep my changes when George updates it"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-02-keep-your-changes.md): Change an app someone else made, with a reason each time, and keep every change through their update
- [3. Ivan's agents: "Give each run a hub of its own, and throw it away afterwards"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-03-a-hub-per-agent-run.md): An agent run in a sandbox starts a hub of its own from a file, leaves its fix as files for review, and the hub is deleted; the team's hub never changes
- [4. A preview on a hub of its own: "Show me what this branch would do to production, and let me see it running"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-04-preview-a-change.md): What a new version would do to production, then seen running with Argo CD on a local cluster, with nothing left behind
- [6. Ivan: "Show me what is actually running, and who changed what"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-06-what-runs-and-why.md): Which customer changed what, whether anyone said why, and who breaks the image rule, one command each across every customer
- [7. The customer, months later: "Take the platform's next version, and keep the change we had to make"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-07-next-version.md): Take a platform's next version, about a hundred changes, and keep the one value you set on purpose, with its reason
- [8. An agent's own configuration: "Give every team the assistant, and let each keep what it changed"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-08-agent-config.md): Each team keeps its own changes to a shared AI assistant through the next version, with the evaluation that explains them
- [9. Dan at ACME: "What is where, and what is running?"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-09-git-hub-and-running.md): Git, the hub and the cluster side by side, each difference sorted, and the app handed back to Git without a restart
- [10. Each person on a key of their own, and moving up to the organization's ConfigHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-10-a-key-each.md): Three parties, a key each made by its holder, and everything outside each one's part refused
- [11. The whole path: from an agent in Claude Code to a bank's fleet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-11-propose-not-approve.md): An agent proposes a change to production and is refused when it tries to approve it; production changes only with your yes
- [12. The devlab: one developer, a laptop, agents, and the hubs it connects to](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-12-laptop-connects-out.md): A laptop hub that nothing connects to, and your work copied up to the team's hosted hub with its reasons
- [13. Sam's first hour: from the page to a gate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-13-first-hour.md): The plugin and a hub on your laptop, with no account: production behind your approval, and an agent's own approval refused
- [14. Sam's VM: a service that takes its settings from the hub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-14-sam-vm.md): A service's folder written only from approved settings; the agent holds a hub key and nothing that reaches the service
- [15. The telling: the three things you are told](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-15-the-telling.md): A change waiting for you, an agent proposing again what you refused, and a hub something elsewhere cannot reach: and nothing else
- [16. Sam's app platform on one hub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-16-app-platform.md): An agent proposes a release, you approve it, the runtime takes it, and you roll it back in one command
- [17. The portal is the agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-17-the-portal.md): What runs and why, what breaks a rule, what a key may change, and a new service from a tested one, each one question to the hub
- [18. Ana asks for an app, and it fits the pattern](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-18-dev-intent.md): A new app on the team's pattern, with rules that keep a value over the limit from reaching the service, and a second app made from the first
- [19. Sam's bad afternoon: stop it, find it, undo it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-19-recovery.md): One command stops every agent session and takes an agent's key away; then find its change and put it back
- [20. Noor's staging: more memory, and production left alone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-20-noors-staging.md): An agent changes staging's own file; production changes only with your approval
- [22. Priya approves from Slack, and it counts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-22-priya-slack.md): Told in the Slack thread where the work was asked for; your Approve there hands you one command that records the approval as yours, and anyone else's press approves nothing (local Slack stand-in)
- [23. Theo's first app: the setup travels with it from the first prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-23-theo-first-app.md): The reason for each setting an agent writes, kept with it from the first file, and where the app came from
- [24. Priya's platform team's base: one base, ten apps, one bump](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-24-company-base.md): One change to a shared base reaches every app, and each app keeps the values it set itself
- [25. Alice ships it, Bob hardens it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/story-25-alice-bob-hardened.md): A reviewer's fixes become the starter's next version: the next app starts with them, the first app takes them

## Get started

- [Walkthroughs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/walkthroughs/README.md): One job from start to finish for each tool, starter and user story, with every command and what it prints
- [Try the plugin on its own](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/try-the-plugin.md): See the record at work, with no hub; what it records, and setting it up for your whole team
- [A new app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/journeys/new-app.md): One request in Claude Code gives you the app, with staging and production settings in a hub
- [An app you already have](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/journeys/existing-app.md): Attach `.env` files, Terraform var files, Kustomize or Helm values, with your values kept as they are
- [An app that Argo CD or Flux deploys](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/journeys/gitops-app.md): A hub beside Git, a check on each pull request, or the hub as the app's source, and the way back
- [Install confighub mini](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/install-mini.md): The hub on your laptop, free and with no account: from Claude Code in one step, or on its own without the plugin; upgrading and removing it
- [A first run of confighub mini](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/try-confighub-mini.md): Install it, try one story, put your agents' record into the hub, and tell us how it went

## Concepts

- [When ConfigHub acts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/agent-workflow.md): Why ordinary coding requests don't start a hub, the one question the plugin may ask you, and where your app runs
- [How the plugin works](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/how-it-works.md): What agents are told and when, what's recorded and what never is, every setting, and the tokens each change cost
- [Approvals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/approvals.md): An agent proposes a change to production and only the person you name approves it, including when one agent asks another for a change
- [Starters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/starters.md): Your team's default settings for every new app. Your own values always win. Off unless you switch them on
- [From your laptop to a shared hub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/from-plugin-to-confighub.md): Each step from the plugin to confighub mini to your organization's ConfigHub, and what it adds
- [Agents that run for weeks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/agents-that-run-for-weeks.md): A key for each agent, approval of the exact change, stopping an agent, and limiting what it can reach
- [Signed records](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/signed-records.md): Checking that nobody tampered with the record, and having each agent sign its own changes

## Reference

- [cub mini and plain cub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/cub-mini-and-cub.md): Which ConfigHub commands each `cub mini` command stands for
- [What a repository deploys](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/inventory.md): `/confighub:inventory`: each app and chart, and what deploys it
- [Working with the tools you already have](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/integrations.md): What the plugin does with each tool, and how far along each one is
- [Going back](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/journeys/going-back.md): Undoing a step, taking your apps out as plain files, and removing each part
- [Limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/limits.md): What the plugin and confighub mini don't do, or haven't been shown to do

## Other tools and setups

- [Codex](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/codex.md): The one setup command Codex needs
- [CI and sandboxes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/ci-and-sandboxes.md): The plugin in a job or a container, and keeping its record after the sandbox is deleted
- [Agents in CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/ci/README.md): GitHub Actions jobs that run a coding agent, from the plugin alone to an agent whose changes a person approves
- [Git and GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/git-and-github.md): The plugin with Git and GitHub, `/confighub:to-hub`, and a hub beside Git
- [The pull-request review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/review/README.md): A comment on each pull request with every setting it changes, and why; no hub needed
- [Entire](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/entire.md): If you use [Entire](https://entire.io): `entire confighub why` gives the reason for a value, with each session's Entire checkpoint
- [A service on a VM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/vm.md): A service's files written from the hub, with only approved values
- [A Helm chart you use, with your values](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/your-own-chart.md): Keep your own values, each with its reason, through a vendor chart's next version
- [GitOps over OCI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/gitops-over-oci.md): Flux and Argo CD deploying what the hub approved
- [Software with ConfigHub inside](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/journeys/bundled.md): An app, platform or chart that comes with a hub: what exists today and what doesn't
- [Runnable examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/roadmap/README.md): A service on a VM with approval and rollback, settings reused across apps, and copying an app between hubs and back to plain files
- [Extensions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/extensions/config-snapshot/README.md): A small program that reads one version of an app's settings from a hub, and an [experimental add-on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/examples/extensions/delivery/README.md) that delivers an approved version outside Kubernetes

## How this was tested

- [Testing the plugin and confighub mini](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/testing.md): Runnable checks, comparisons, and every dated run record
- [What agents did with the plugin and without it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/docs/evidence.md): Real sessions, quoted as the agents wrote them
- [Evaluate it yourself](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confighubai/confighub-mini-plugin/main/evaluate/README.md): The same evaluation, with your own models, in one command
